description: simulate a construction file — resolve every named oligo and plasmid across the whole project folder, run the steps, report each product and its length, and say whether a sequencing primer actually sits inside that product and has only one site
phrases: does this PCR give the right product
does the sequencing primer anneal in the PCR product
is the sequencing oligo inside that pcr product
how big is the PCR product
does the simulated plasmid match the recorded map
check a primer for a second binding site

requires.note: parseCF and simCF — the simulator itself
resolves the named inputs across the project, including sequences that exist only inside a labsheet workbook

returns: one line per product with its length in bp; the named inputs that resolved nowhere; and with --primes, where that oligo sits in each product and whether it binds more than once. Exit 1 when a step failed
notes: Complements cf.check, which reads a construction file's structure and deliberately never asks whether the chemistry works. Resolution is project-wide because a construction file's inputs live wherever they were made — SynThera's pGhost16 takes one template from SLIP4 and another from SLIP3 — and because some sequences exist only in a labsheet workbook and in no ordering sheet at all. --primes answers the question that follows every simulated PCR and had no tool: a primer with two binding sites gives an unreadable trace and nothing structural can see it. On an annealing failure it measures each primer's longest 3'-anchored exact match against simCF's 18 nt rule, because a mutagenic primer whose designed base falls inside that window is rejected by the simulator and still works at the bench.
